author: Kevin Kelly
short: Private local dashboard with music, explained settings and all-cog data views.
description: Self-contained responsive web dashboard hosted inside Red with aiohttp. Private single-use owner codes, bounded expiring sessions, CSRF/origin/host checks, server/channel selection, music controls and 32 explained settings. Searchable paginated read-only datasets across all fourteen loaded suite cogs include intro owners, activity, XP, rewards, listening history, collections and reviewed operational records. Data reads retain originating command/source permissions and add no duplicate database. Changes invoke real Red command parsing, checks, hooks and cooldowns. Optional SettingsHub themes/audits apply. Listener defaults off on loopback; bind/port/start/displayed URL policy persist across restarts. No separate Node.js service, bot-token input, raw Config view or external hosting required.
install_msg: Use [p]load dashboardplus, [p]dashboard start and [p]dashboard login. Default URL: http://127.0.0.1:8765. For Docker stop it, bind 0.0.0.0 8765 and publish port 8765, then start it. Save the displayed link with [p]dashboard url http://YOUR-RED-HOST:8765/. Owner-only controls; login code goes by DM or ephemeral /dashboard login. Guide: https://github.com/kevinwaynekelly/kevin-cogs/blob/main/dashboardplus/README.md
end_user_data_statement: Stores only listener enabled/bind/port, displayed URL and allowed hostnames in Red Config. Codes/session hashes, CSRF tokens, owner IDs and expiry times remain in bounded memory and expire/revoke on stop/unload/restart. No bot token, password, duplicate member database or web access history is saved. Owners can read reviewed settings, public track metadata and selected source-cog records such as activity, XP, intros and history, subject to current source permissions. Read-only views do not alter source retention or create a separate persistent copy. Source cogs retain their own data/audit policies. User-data hooks export credential-free transient login counts and revoke that user's logins.
